rename.from: [TurboPack] No Media Queries breakpoints in Chrome Device Emulation mode
rename.to: [Turbopack] No Media Queries breakpoints in Chrome Device Emulation mode

body: Turns out the problem is that Lightingcss (in Turbopack) minifies @media, but if you set `experimental: { turbo: { useSwcCss: true } }` in the config to disable it, everything displays.
That flag is legacy and will be removed in an upcoming patch release. We'll want to figure out why LightningCSS is causing problems for this case 🙂

LightningCSS apparently always (if supported by your `browserslist` config) turns `(max-width: 768px)` into `(width <= 768px)`.
That makes sense when minification is enabled because this save a few bytes. But unfortunately Chrome doesn't visualize that.
[Example](https://lightningcss.dev/playground/index.html#%7B%22minify%22%3Afalse%2C%22customMedia%22%3Atrue%2C%22cssModules%22%3Afalse%2C%22analyzeDependencies%22%3Afalse%2C%22targets%22%3A%7B%22chrome%22%3A7864320%7D%2C%22include%22%3A0%2C%22exclude%22%3A0%2C%22source%22%3A%22%40media%20screen%20and%20(max-width%3A%20768px)%20%7B%5Cn%20%20body%20%7B%5Cn%20%20%20%20color%3A%20red%3B%5Cn%20%20%7D%5Cn%7D%22%2C%22visitorEnabled%22%3Afalse%2C%22visitor%22%3A%22%7B%5Cn%20%20Color(color)%20%7B%5Cn%20%20%20%20if%20(color.type%20%3D%3D%3D%20'rgb')%20%7B%5Cn%20%20%20%20%20%20color.g%20%3D%200%3B%5Cn%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20color%3B%5Cn%20%20%20%20%7D%5Cn%20%20%7D%5Cn%7D%22%2C%22unusedSymbols%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22version%22%3A%22local%22%7D)

Today, I noticed that my CSS media queries don't work on iPhone SE (15.8.3) (Safari/Firefox). After a few hours, a complete project configuration overhaul, and a ton of lost hair, I finally traced the issue to the `next dev --turbopack` flag. Then I managed to find this issue, so I won't create a duplicate.

As @mischnic mentioned, the CSS gets transformed, and I believe the resulting state is likely too modern and not supported by the rendering engine.

`@media (max-device-width: 1000px)` turns into `@media (device-width <= 1000px)`
 `@media (max-width: 1000px)` turns into `@media (width <= 1000px)`

I can confirm that `experimental: { turbo: { useSwcCss: true } }` works. However, @timneutkens, if you plan to remove this option and potentially enable support for `next build`, as stated here https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/2161d8c012dcd98eb8690814bd275d56c45bf00a/docs/03-architecture/turbopack.mdx?plain=1#L29 is there a convenient way to configure LightningCSS in Next.js for those who will want to target older devices? Or should they simply be aware of this and disable `--turbopack` in the production build?

Interestingly, when I use `@media (device-width <= 1000px)` in my SCSS file and build the project with `next build`, it gets transformed into `@media (max-device-width: 1000px)`.

As a workaround, Next.js could override the  [MediaRangeSyntax](https://docs.rs/lightningcss/latest/lightningcss/targets/struct.Features.html#associatedconstant.MediaRangeSyntax) feature in lightningcss (to force LightningCSS to not use it even if supported by the browserslist config)
Starting with Next.js 15.1 they removed `experimental: { turbo: { useSwcCss: true } }`

issue.title: Turbopack: Disable LightningCSS MediaRangeSyntax feature
issue.body:
## What?

Always downlevels MediaRangeSyntax to ensure max-width doesn't get upleveled to MediaRangeSyntax which is shorter but doesn't work with Chrome devtools `show media queries` feature.

Fixes #72559

Closes PACK-5723
